question: A 40-year-old male from rural Rajasthan presents with a 3-year history of progressive nasal obstruction, foul-smelling crusting, and a firm painless mass filling the nasal cavity and extending to the upper lip. Biopsy shows Mikulicz cells (large foamy macrophages containing intracellular organisms) and Russell bodies. What is the most likely diagnosis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nasal TB shows caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells and acid-fast bacilli on ZN stain — not Mikulicz cells or Russell bodies.

Correct. Rhinoscleroma is caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis and is pathognomonic for Mikulicz cells (large vacuolated macrophages stuffed with bacilli) and Russell bodies (hyaline inclusions in plasma cells). It progresses through catarrhal, proliferative (granulomatous), and cicatricial (scarring) stages, causing the characteristic hard nasal mass and eventually nasal stenosis.
GPA shows necrotising granulomas with vasculitis on biopsy, positive c-ANCA/PR3, and causes septal perforation and saddle-nose deformity — not Mikulicz cells.

Rhinosporidiosis (Rhinosporidium seeberi) shows large sporangia containing endospores on biopsy. It presents as a friable, vascular, strawberry-like polyp — not a hard infiltrating mass with Mikulicz cells.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the histological signatures of granulomatous nasal diseases. Mikulicz cells (foamy macrophages with intracellular bacilli) + Russell bodies = rhinoscleroma (Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis). This distinguishes it from TB (caseating granuloma + AFB), GPA (necrotising vasculitis + c-ANCA), and rhinosporidiosis (sporangia with endospores).
Excellent. Mikulicz cells and Russell bodies are the hallmark of rhinoscleroma. This triad — hard nasal mass, Mikulicz cells on biopsy, Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis — must be recalled as a unit.
